The 721 MB stage2_work cache was left on the cluster per the user's instruction; only 1.3 MB of analysed results came home. Stage-1 evidence in the same directory verified byte-identical (not overwritten).

CORRECTED after independent review (the review is authoritative over my earlier note; see the review record):

H1 IS UNTESTED, NOT SUPPORTED. The mesh comparison and the replicate baseline are NOT commensurable. convergence_stage2.py:244 and :258 build the design cases for EVERY mesh from the same seed-101 draws, so the mesh comparison has ZERO case-draw variability; :274 builds each replicate from a DIFFERENT draw (seeds 1101-1108), so the baseline carries full case-draw variability. The baseline therefore contains a variance component the mesh comparison does not, and a one-sided mesh<=baseline test cannot fail: a deliberately broken 2 km mesh would also pass. Confirmed in the data: all 48 vs_main regret rows are positive (in-sample vs out-of-sample advantage), median 0.95-2.51 x J_ref, against mesh-induced |regret| of 0.068-0.115 x J_ref.

CRITERION: the registered rule tests IQR_low <= x <= IQR_high while the hypothesis says 'no larger than', so the registered rule yields NO verdict on H1. All 6 failures are below-the-floor, never above-the-ceiling. This is a POST-HOC repair found after seeing results, not a reinterpretation, and must be registered as a dated amendment. Correction to my earlier note: at noise 0.05 budget 5 the displacement was INSIDE the IQR (2771 in [2565,3673]); only regret failed low, so 'failed in all six cells for the same reason' was wrong.

TEST RESULT RETRACTED. The '6-35% better on held-out test' claim is a single-case artefact: n=6 cases (not 18 rows; 6 cases x 3 noise reps), case 0 carries the headline, leave-one-out drops budget 3 from -26.5% to -4.0% and budget 5 from -35.3% to -8.7%, sign counts 4/6, Wilcoxon p=0.22-0.56. Correct reading: NO DETECTABLE DIFFERENCE.

'OBJECTIVE IS VERY FLAT' RETRACTED - MIS-DIAGNOSED. eps_sd/J_ref is 1.01-2.52 at noise 0.05, i.e. the tie threshold is LARGER than the objective itself, so tie_fraction does not measure flatness. At f0.05 b8, 319/368 swaps degrade J by >10% of J_ref and the median degradation is +30%, yet 367/368 are labelled tied. The real problem is that the design objective is NOT IDENTIFIABLE at 6 cases. Budget 8 / noise 0.05 must be excluded from stability claims.

'dt HAS NO EFFECT' OVER-SCOPED: true for dt 100 vs 50 only; dt 25 was never run and has no stop clause. The 125 m arm was dropped although its registered stop condition (250 m stage exceeding 4 h) was NOT met - an undeclared deviation.

NEW FINDING NOT PREVIOUSLY FLAGGED: mesh regret is NEGATIVE at noise 0.05 (-6.8% to -11.5% of J_ref), falsifying numerical-methodology.md section 5's non-negativity expectation and bounding greedy sub-optimality at >=7-12% at the reference mesh. So 'regret vs the reference layout' partly measures greedy path-dependence, and this benignly explains the apparent test advantage.

Budgets 3/5/8 are NESTED PREFIXES of one greedy trace (convergence_stage2.py:176-177), so the effective number of independent decision comparisons is 2 (one per noise fraction), not 6. Noise 0.15 is UNINFORMATIVE for mesh (sampling noise ~1.3 x J_ref swamps the mesh difference). Verified clean by the reviewer: no test-set leakage (:289 asserts layouts exist before :293 builds test cases), alpha is an exact-equality assert against the frozen file (:150-156), noise scale frozen (:142-147), ensembles machine-checked disjoint, fresh seed 304 never used.
